studies.title: Salvage City Supper Club
studies.venueDetail: Nomads Land, Las Vegas Motor Speedway
studies.alt: Supper club table set for service
studies.description: Salvage City Supper Club, a post-apocalyptic immersive dinner show inside EDC Las Vegas: a 60-minute, five-course seated experience with a dozen performers, run inside a working festival footprint.
studies.keywords: premium hospitality case study, festival hospitality production, immersive dinner show, EDC Las Vegas, Nomads Land, supper club production
studies.lede: A five-course, sixty-minute immersive dinner show running inside a working festival footprint at EDC Las Vegas, installed, run, and struck on the festival's clock.
facts: A dozen performers working the room
studies.challenge: Insomniac needed a premium seated experience that could live inside EDC Las Vegas without competing with it, a fully realised world guests felt they had stumbled onto, sited in Nomads Land, inside a festival footprint with its own identity, its own technical constraints, and an audience that has seen everything. The constraints were real: a fixed footprint, a hard load-in window against the festival's own build, and a guest experience that had to stay intimate while turning over night after night.
studies.approach:
The full production lifecycle, Discover through Close. Discover defined the narrative world and tested it against the site. Design delivered the scenic language; Advance cleared the build against venue and fire-code requirements and locked the schedule around the festival calendar.
Procure and Build fabricated a modular scenic package sized to the load-in window. Install sequenced crew and freight around live programming. Operate ran the room on service, a choreographed show moving around seated guests while five courses landed on time. Close returned the ground clean.
studies.pull: A world guests felt they'd stumbled onto, installed and run and struck on the festival's clock.
studies.result: The format returned to EDC Las Vegas, the clearest result an experience like this can post, and the reason the trade write-ups lead on returns to rather than debuts at. Salvage City is now a repeatable format: proof that a seated, catered, performed world can be delivered inside a live festival footprint without either one compromising the other. Attendance and sell-through figures publish here as they clear client review.

studies.title: L-Acoustics DJ
studies.alt: Audio control surface in a live sound control room
studies.description: L-Acoustics DJ at III Points, Miami, the first US festival deployment of L-Acoustics' spatial audio system for DJs, on the S3QU3NC3 stage at Mana Wynwood, October 2025.
studies.keywords: L-Acoustics DJ, spatial audio festival, S3QU3NC3 stage, III Points Miami, immersive audio implementation, L-ISA, event technology implementation
studies.lede: The first US festival deployment of L-Acoustics DJ, real-time spatial audio on the S3QU3NC3 stage at III Points, Mana Wynwood, October 2025.
facts: Four stacks of three KS28, cardioid
studies.challenge: III Points has treated sound system design as part of its identity for nearly a decade, running L-Acoustics on every stage for eight consecutive years. In 2024 the festival brought L-ISA to North American festival audiences on the 444 stage. For 2025 the brief went further: put L-Acoustics DJ, the first complete spatial audio system built for DJs, in front of a festival crowd for the first time in the United States. That is a different problem from hanging a bigger system. Spatial playback has to hold up across a ninety-by-ninety-foot two-level room, for artists who have never touched it, on a festival schedule that does not pause for a soundcheck.
studies.approach:
Technology and systems work across Advance, Procure, Install and Operate. Advance resolved the design against the structure and the schedule. Install brought up eight hangs of L2D in an 8.1 configuration, four frontal stacks of three KS28 in cardioid for low frequency control, and a ring of six coaxial X12 with two KS21i overhead for the immersive monitor mix.
Operate is where the implementation is decided. The system separates a stereo mix into its elements in real time and hands an artist spatial control over them, so the work is as much artist enablement as it is rigging: a default spatialisation mode carried performers who did not want to drive it live, and the ones who did got the room.
studies.pull: Not listening to music. Being inside it.
studies.result: The live-sound trades picked it up: FOH and Mix both carried it, alongside AVNation and USITT. So did the artists who played it. Kujo, one of the DJs selected for the system, walked through the preparation and the in-set decisions with Magnetic Magazine afterwards. III Points returns in 2026, and the open question the trades keep asking is the useful one: which stage adopts spatial audio next, and whether the format travels beyond electronic music.

studies.title: Black Coffee at the Race Track
studies.alt: Open-air crowd at a racetrack show at dusk
studies.description: Black Coffee at the Race Track, the first dance music event ever staged at Hialeah Park, the 1922 racetrack, presented by Club Space for Miami Music Week 2026 with Carlita and Kaz James.
studies.keywords: Hialeah Park racetrack event, Black Coffee Miami, Miami Music Week 2026, Club Space, open-air festival production, racetrack event production
studies.lede: The first dance music event ever staged at Hialeah Park, an open-air build on a 1922 racetrack, presented by Club Space for Miami Music Week 2026.
facts: First dance music event at the track
studies.challenge:
Hialeah Park is a landmark, not a venue. Opened in 1922 and redesigned in the thirties around gardens and flamingo pools, it had never hosted a dance music event, which meant there was no infrastructure to inherit and no precedent to copy. Everything an open-air show needs had to be brought in and taken back out.
And the site came with a constraint no production rider covers: the park's flamingos, imported from Cuba in 1934, had to be kept away from the music and otherwise undisturbed.
studies.approach:
A greenfield build on a protected site. Discover and Design worked the sightlines and the sound against a listed landscape rather than a bare field. Advance carried the permissions and the site-specific conditions, including the exclusion zones that kept the wildlife clear of the programme.
Procure, Build and Install put in a temporary open-air venue on the infield and took it back out. Operate ran a seven-hour show from six until one; Close returned the park to the condition a 1922 landmark is handed back in.
studies.pull: A hundred-year-old racetrack, open air, for one night.
studies.result: The show ran, the flamingos were undisturbed, and the coverage led on the thing that mattered: a historic track hosting dance music for the first time. BizBash carried it in its Miami Music Week round-up, Miami New Times and Time Out previewed it, and World Red Eye shot the night. The result worth having is not the attendance figure. It is that a landmark that had never done this now has a template for doing it again.

studies.title: The Polymarket
studies.venueDetail: 7th Avenue at Charles Street, Lower Manhattan
studies.alt: Produce aisle stocked in a grocery store
studies.description: The Polymarket: New York's first free grocery store, a fully stocked five-day retail activation in the West Village where every shopper filled a tote at no cost, alongside a $1M donation to Food Bank For New York City.
studies.keywords: Polymarket free grocery store, West Village pop-up, retail activation New York, brand activation case study, experiential retail production
studies.lede: A fully stocked grocery store in the West Village, open to anyone, where nothing had a price, five days, no purchase, no catch.
facts: A tote per shopper, filled free
$1M to Food Bank For New York City
studies.challenge:
Build a working grocery store in Lower Manhattan, in February, and operate it as a real shop for five days, stocked, staffed, queued and restocked, where nothing scans and nobody pays. Retail operations with the transaction removed and the demand unknowable.
A free store in a city with a food-insecurity problem draws a crowd that is not a marketing audience. The build had to hold a queue on a West Village street, in winter, without turning the thing it was trying to do into a spectacle at the expense of the people in it.
studies.approach:
Retail build and site operations run as one job. Design and Advance handled the storefront, the fit-out and the street: sightlines, queue management, the permissions that a five-day operating shop needs rather than the ones a pop-up gets away with.
Build and Install fitted a functioning store, shelving, cold chain, back of house, restock cadence. Operate is the whole of a project like this: crowd flow, a guaranteed allocation for the first three hundred in line each day, restocking against demand nobody could forecast, and a queue kept orderly and warm on a public street.
studies.pull: Retail operations with the transaction taken out.
studies.result: Thousands were served on the first day, and the store ran its full five days. Polymarket donated $1 million to Food Bank For New York City and three million meals alongside it. The coverage was national: Newsweek, Fox Business, FOX 5, Vice. It was not uniformly warm. Some of it was politically framed and some questioned the motive. That is the honest record of a free grocery store in an election-year news cycle, and it is worth stating plainly: the queue was the story, in both directions.

studies.title: Factory Town
studies.alt: Crowd in a warehouse venue under structural lighting
studies.description: Factory Town, Hialeah, venue and site operations across a seven-acre open-air entertainment district built in a 1946 mattress factory, run season after season through Miami Music Week and Art Basel.
studies.keywords: Factory Town Miami, Hialeah venue operations, warehouse venue production, Miami Music Week, Art Basel Miami events, multi-stage site operations
studies.lede: Seven acres of industrial Hialeah, a 1946 factory floor and the land around it, run as a multi-stage open-air venue season after season.
facts: Miami Music Week and Art Basel
studies.challenge:
Factory Town is not a room with a calendar. It is a seven-acre site in Hialeah built around an abandoned mattress factory, the Dixie Bedding plant, put up in 1946 and once a US Army contractor, with a large open-sided warehouse and a great deal of open ground where stages and structures go up and come down.
Operating it means the venue is rebuilt for its programme rather than booked into. Every season the site changes shape: different stage counts, different capacities, different circulation, on ground that is industrial rather than purpose-built.
studies.approach:
Venue and site operations, run as a standing discipline rather than a series of one-offs. Logistics and workforce planning against a footprint that moves. Vendor coordination across a site with no permanent back of house. Health, safety and compliance on an industrial property. Day-of operations across multiple stages running at once.
The repeatable part is the standard, not the layout: the same nine phases applied to every season, so a Miami Music Week build and an Art Basel build differ in shape but not in how they are run, gated or closed out.
studies.pull: The venue gets rebuilt for the programme, not booked into.
studies.result:
Season after season across 2023–25, through Miami Music Week and Art Basel, for headline programmes including Black Coffee, Solomun, Elrow, ZHU, Dom Dolla and Green Velvet.
World Red Eye has photographed the site for years and keeps a standing archive of it, the closest thing to a continuous public record of what the ground has held.

studies.title: Heineken Turn 4 Nightclub
studies.description: Heineken Turn 4 Nightclub, a nightclub-format hospitality space built trackside at Turn 4 for the 2024 Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix, running across the full race weekend.
studies.keywords: F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix hospitality, Turn 4 club, Heineken activation, motorsport hospitality production, trackside nightclub build
studies.lede: A nightclub built trackside at Turn 4 for the 2024 Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix, running the full race weekend on the Koval Straightaway.
studies.challenge:
A Formula 1 street circuit is the least forgiving build environment in live events. The Las Vegas Grand Prix runs on live city roads, on a schedule the FIA sets and nobody negotiates, with a build and a strike measured against track access windows rather than convenience.
The brief was a nightclub, a room with the sound, the lighting and the service standard of a permanent venue, sited at Turn 4 and holding its own against a Grand Prix happening on the other side of the barrier.
studies.approach:
Design and Advance worked to the circuit's calendar first and the venue's second: access windows, load paths, and the compliance regime a live motorsport circuit imposes on everything inside it. Procure and Build packaged a room that could be installed in the time the track allowed.
Install and Operate ran to the race schedule across three days, with the guest experience holding through track sessions rather than around them. Close struck to the circuit's timetable, which on a street course is the deadline that actually matters.
studies.pull: A permanent venue's standard, built to a street circuit's clock.
studies.result: The room ran across the 21–23 November race weekend. BizBash included the weekend's Turn 4 hospitality in its round-up of the standout activations at the 2024 Grand Prix, the trade read by the people who commission this work. The promoter's own wrap-up called the 2024 race a new standard for the event.

studies.title: Red Bull Unforeseen Motel
studies.alt: Weathered neon MOTEL sign lit at dusk
studies.description: Red Bull Unforeseen Motel, a motel-world brand environment built inside III Points at Mana Wynwood, Miami, 2024, programmed with Club Space residents and local artists rather than a logo on a stage.
studies.keywords: Red Bull Unforeseen, III Points Miami 2024, Mana Wynwood, brand activation case study, festival brand environment, Club Space residents
studies.lede: A motel built inside a festival: Red Bull's environment at III Points 2024, programmed with Club Space residents and Miami locals instead of a logo on a stage.
studies.challenge:
A brand at a music festival usually buys a stage and puts its name on it. The brief here was the opposite: build somewhere that would have been worth going to without the logo, inside III Points at Mana Wynwood, and let the programming rather than the branding do the work.
That sets a harder bar. A motel-world environment has to read as a place from the moment someone walks in, hold a crowd across two festival days, and sit inside a festival footprint that is already competing for the same attention.
studies.approach:
Design built the world, a motel, rendered fully enough to behave like one rather than to photograph like one. Advance and Install sited and built it inside the III Points footprint against the festival's own build schedule.
The programming was the point and was curated as such: eight Club Space residents and more than a dozen local artists, including back-to-back pairings, with III Points' own leadership on the line-up. Operate ran it across both festival days.
studies.pull: Somewhere worth going without the logo on it.
studies.result:
The Motel ran across both days of the 2024 festival at Mana Wynwood, curated with III Points' own leadership rather than around them, and World Red Eye's gallery of the edition is the visual record.
It worked well enough to come back: Red Bull returned the Unforeseen Motel to III Points the following year. Ours is the 2024 build.

studies.title: PATRÓN Cristalino x Becky G
studies.alt: Spirit poured over ice in a rocks glass
studies.description: PATRÓN Cristalino x Becky G, the US launch of PATRÓN Cristalino on Olvera Street, Los Angeles, September 2024, with Becky G, Gabito Ballesteros and Tito Double P.
studies.keywords: PATRON Cristalino launch, Becky G, Olvera Street Los Angeles, product launch event production, spirits launch activation, Musica Mexicana event
studies.lede: The US launch of PATRÓN Cristalino, staged on Olvera Street, a tasting, a dinner and a live show with Becky G, Gabito Ballesteros and Tito Double P.
facts: Becky G, Gabito Ballesteros, Tito Double P
First time the three performed together
studies.challenge: A spirits launch on Olvera Street, the oldest street in Los Angeles and the heart of the city's Mexican-American history, is a cultural venue before it is an event site. Get the register wrong and a brand launch on that ground reads as appropriation rather than celebration. The brief was a US product launch that worked as a cultural moment: an intimate tasting, a paired menu, and a live show, on a public historic street, for an audience and a press corps who would notice immediately if it were hollow.
studies.approach:
Design and Advance handled a build on a historic public street, access, permissions, and a room that had to feel intimate on ground that is not private. Procure and Build delivered the tasting environment and the stage.
Talent and show management ran the performance side: Becky G headlining with an unreleased single alongside her catalogue, and the first joint appearance with Gabito Ballesteros and Tito Double P, a booking that only works if the run-of-show and the artist logistics hold. The evening opened on a tasting of Añejo and Cristalino paired with chocolates and tacos, then moved to the show.
studies.pull: A launch that had to read as a celebration, not a takeover.
studies.result: The most broadly and warmly covered project in the archive. WWD ran a photo gallery, ¡HOLA! covered the Selena tribute, and The Knockturnal, Loop, LA Guestlist and identify LA all filed from the night. Every piece led on the performances and the cultural framing rather than the product, which, for a launch, is the result.

studies.title: FIFA World Cup Brazil Base Camp
studies.description: FIFA World Cup Brazil Base Camp, team base camp operations in New Jersey for the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
studies.keywords: World Cup 2026 base camp, team base camp operations, New Jersey, sporting event operations, tournament hospitality production
studies.lede: Base camp operations in New Jersey for the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
studies.challenge: A tournament base camp is a closed operation with a fixed occupant and no margin. It runs to a calendar set by the competition, with security, media and access regimes that are not negotiable, for a party whose only interest in the site is that it never becomes a distraction.
studies.approach: Venue and site operations across the tournament window: logistics, workforce, vendor coordination, and the compliance and access control a tournament imposes, planned in Advance, run in Operate, closed out clean.
studies.pull: A base camp works when nobody notices it.
studies.result: Details publish here as the tournament progresses and as they clear approval.
